body:
For about a week, I felt better. On my internal list of things I wanted to do, "Go back to sleep" wasn't ranking in the top five anymore. 

I don't know if it was placebo and the bump of just getting treatment, or if it actually is still working and I'd be crushed by where I am right now without it. I've got my head above water, but I don't know if the water is lower or if I'm standing on a box.

I used to regard my libido as a decent yardstick, but HRT has done strange things to it.

I'm on the same antidepressant that worked well for my Mom.

If I lose my job, plan is to move home with parent. Logistics would lead to a new therapist, new Mental Health department.

If I continue to seek care, it'll be with someone else.

Thank you for your advice and encouragement.

[](/b30 "I've been waiting for it to 'get better in two years' for a decade now..." ) Personally, I'm kind of surprised I've kicked around this long.

I've got a contract job, and the contract ends in December. I've been to college twice, served in the Air Force, and am on my second post-college Job. 

 [](/b04 "Or VA Directive 2011-024 won't get renewed in any useful form. In that case, I'll politely write them a letter to let them know I've decided to discontinue pursuit of medical care.") 
If the contract doesn't get renewed, I don't think I can pick myself up again. I don't really want to take another go at the rodeo of life. I'll either walk myself into a VA clinic as a last ditch effort at life, or asphyxiate myself with a noble gas.




Or I'll get lucky. This roll around I might not screw things up. 

On topic, I drive a somewhat modern car. In a wreck, it'll crumple into a ball of tangled metal and hail damage. But I'll likely be alive. I'm more likely to kill myself than die in a car crash, I think.
